title: IBM Stock: Buy, Hold, or Sell?

description: IBM management has reiterated revenue targets for the current fiscal year, forecasting 5% revenue growth. title: Better Quantum Computing Stock: IonQ vs. D-Wave
author: Will Healy
description: The article compares two quantum computing stocks, IonQ and D-Wave Quantum. IonQ demonstrates industry-leading precision with 99.99% 2-qubit gate fidelities and has a partnership with Nvidia, but faces massive operating losses and an extremely high P/S ratio of 65. D-Wave has achieved real-world applications through its quantum annealing technology and Leap cloud service, but revenue declined 67% year-over-year with a P/S ratio of 475. The author recommends IonQ as the relatively safer choice despite both stocks carrying significant risks and being overvalued.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: IonQ demonstrates industry-leading technical precision (99.99% gate fidelities), has a strategic partnership with Nvidia providing competitive advantage, and shows strong revenue growth ($145M vs $28M year-over-year). However, sentiment is tempered by massive operating losses ($1.06B) and extremely high valuation (P/S of 65).

D-Wave has achieved notable real-world applications with its quantum annealing technology and Leap cloud service, demonstrating commercial viability ahead of competitors. However, this is significantly offset by declining revenue (-67% YoY), substantial operating losses ($66M), and an extremely high valuation (P/S of 475), making it a risky investment.

Nvidia is mentioned positively as a strategic partner of IonQ, installing IonQ's Superion 256 system at its Accelerated Quantum Research Center, positioning itself at the forefront of quantum computing development.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Life Sciences Market: Trends and Forecast to 2040 | Market to Reach USD 73.05 Billion at 20% CAGR as Drug Discovery and Precision Medicine Scale
